1a: ^The situation is this: inside the hut to my left is a group of branded who have taken a squad of guards hostage. We have confirmed they have killed at least one of them already.

^The strange part is that the branded don't seem keen to negotiate. We only discovered this plot when my men didn't come back from their morning inspection, and any attempt to create a dialogue has ended in stalemate.
^What use are hostages if they aren't used for leverage? Something is wrong here. They're stalling, but we aren't certain for what reason.
^Those leeches! They'll regret this soon, I'm sure.

s: ^Where do we come into this?
^Shut it, Weft.

^So we've decided to force the issue. You two are going to go in there and negotiate for us. I doubt they'd let a guard, even one who is unarmed, enter the hut without taking them hostage as well.

s: ^What guarantee would they have that you would keep your word?

^They were at a cliff's edge and balked at the height. The cowards were glad for a way down.
^This success couldn't have happened without Weft. His words swayed them to peace.
^We were fortunate they believed your offer. Enough doubt and the dealings would have floundered.

c-1: ^That sounds right to me. Branded are always underestimating the hardness of my guards, to their own hazard.

2b: ^That is good to hear. He has served us well before, and I have no doubt will continue to for a long while.
2c: ^This is why rapport with the branded is so important. They're a calculating bunch; you need to get through to them that working with us is how they survive, not against us.
3a: ^The branded you negotiated with were attempting to dig a tunnel out of the camp: hence they needed the hostages to prevent us from attacking them before they could finish.

^The fools thought it would actually succeed. They must have underestimated the distance they would have needed to dig. Even if they had gotten past the walls, the archers in the arrow towers would have picked them off with ease.

s: ^One of them mentioned a 'man made of stone' that attacked them while they were in the tunnel. It kept them from completing it.
^*Say nothing.*

stoneManExplanation: ^A stone saint, surely. They're spirits of the rock that sometimes appear in mines or canyons. We've been lucky not to run into any yet while we dig, but I guess we'll need to be ready if there are more around.
^Stone saints are nasty business. It probably gave the branded a good scare when it came out of the dirt, and was more than the lot of them could handle.
3b: ^Whatever the case, you two have earned a reward for a job well done. I can give you the rest of the extra rations I keep on me right now, and once I inform the Director of what has happened I will ask him to approve something extra.
^You spoil them, Tabor. The other branded will think these two your children if you give them much more.
^Good behaviour should be as visibily rewarded as bad behaviour is punished, Captain. You know how the branded are: the baser comforts can be a better motivator to them than a hundred lashes.
3c: ^We must give our reports to the Director. Once that is done, I will be back to give you two your next task. Take your midday break while I am up in the Manse, then come find me in front of Weft's hut when it is over.
